# Narrative contract

Central question: when does a property made manifest in one representation
count as established for the physical theory represented through an entire
chain of descriptions?

Argumentative chain:

1. Coordinate change, gauge quotient, regulator change, effective
   description, limit, reconstruction, and spectral interpretation are not one
   relation under different names.
2. A representation arrow therefore carries a property-relative certificate:
   exact channels, quantitative moduli, forgotten prerequisites, recovery
   theorems, and explicit uniformity domains.
3. Certificate composition is typed. Exact channels compose conjunctively,
   errors compose with pullback moduli, and a forgotten prerequisite cannot be
   restored by bookkeeping alone.
4. The substantive theorem converts a uniform Euclidean semigroup rate on a
   dense centered recovered core into target spectral exclusion.
5. Hidden sectors, collapsing finite gaps, and noncommuting cutoff/volume
   limits show why completeness and uniformity are physical premises rather
   than stylistic refinements.
6. The Yang--Mills chain distributes locality, gauge invariance, positivity,
   scale dependence, physical time, and spectrum across different
   representations; each interface has its own proof obligation.
7. The framework supports several ontologies but entails none. Its warranted
   conclusion is methodological: physical warrant is proof-bearing coherence
   across relevant representations.

The abstract, introduction, theorem, countermodels, and conclusion all use the
same scope. No passage claims a new continuum construction, OS reconstruction,
or Yang--Mills mass gap.
